name: Oro Win
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.note: Consonant/vowel inventory only; no stress section; cites Ladefoged & Everett 1996, Everett & Kern 1996, Lev-Stark-Chang 2012, Tondineli 2021.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua, Silvania Oro Eo' Cabixi & Luciano Oro Win. 2025. Dicionário Multimídia Oro win-Português, versão 3.0 (preliminar). Belém: Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi. https://dicionarios.museu-goeldi.br/dic/oro_win/
sources.note: No prose statement on stress (the 'Alfabeto' panel is an empty placeholder; the introduction refers readers to the primer Woraw Fet Ti for the alphabet and grammar). The phonetic transcriptions do mark stress: of 106 unique entries on the saved page, 116 orthographic words carry a stress mark and all 116 have it on the final syllable (e.g. /awakiʔ/ [awa'kiʔ], /karapakan/ [karapa'kan], /sakaworita/ [sakawori'ta], /ipijam teke/ [ipi'jam te'ke]); 0 non-final (extracted to). Site asks that this preliminary version not be used for academic research or redistributed.

sources.citation: Galucio, Ana Vilacy, Joshua Birchall, Ivan Rocha et al. 2025. Dicionários multimídia: uma tecnologia social para auxiliar a aprendizagem e revitalização de línguas minorizadas. SciELO Preprints, doi:10.1590/SciELOPreprints.13693 (published Revista da ABRALIN 24(2), 2026)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Section 2.3 describes the Dicionário Oro Win project (858 entries in v3.0, each with orthographic, phonemic and phonetic transcription) and gives the dictionary URL.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua & Olivia Oro Win Cabixi. 2021. Passos na retomada da língua do povo Oro Win. In Patrícia Goulart Tondineli (org.), (Re)vitalizar línguas minorizadas e/ou ameaçadas: teorias, metodologias, pesquisas e experiências, 69-82. Porto Velho: EDUFRO. doi:10.47209/978-65-87539-61-4
sources.note: Nothing on stress (no 'acento', 'sílaba', 'tônica' in the chapter). Sociolinguistic history and revitalization; p. 75 reports that França 2002 is a formal phonological description (tese de doutorado, UNIR Guajará-Mirim, 244 f.) and Popky 1999 an MA thesis (Pittsburgh, 63 f.) built on Everett's 1994 elicitations; refs also list the primer Birchall & Oro Win 2012 'Woraw Fet Ti'!' (manuscript) and Birchall 2018 INDL report.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua, Michael Dunn & Simon J. Greenhill. 2016. A combined comparative and phylogenetic analysis of the Chapacuran language family. International Journal of American Linguistics 82(3): 255-284. doi:10.1086/687383
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (grep: stress/accent/prosod/penult give only a d'Orbigny quote about 'accent' = dialect). Comparative sound correspondences only. p. 261 note on sources: 'De França (2002) presents a phonetic and phonological analysis of the language. The primary source of data comes from field notes collected by Joshua Birchall between 2009 and 2011.'

sources.citation: Lev, Michael, Tammy Stark & Will Chang. 2012. Phonological inventory of Oro Win. South American Phonological Inventory Database (SAPHON), UC Berkeley. https://linguistics.berkeley.edu/~saphon/en/inv/
sources.note: 18 segments; field 'Suprasegmental: None'; sources Popky 1999 and Joshua Birchall p.c.; no statement about stress placement.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua & Antonio Brito. 2011. Oro Win. Povos Indígenas no Brasil (Instituto Socioambiental). https://pib.socioambiental.org/pt/Povo:Oro_Win
sources.note: Nothing on stress; the 'Língua' section covers classification, speaker numbers and Wari' contact effects only.

sources.citation: Birchall, Joshua. 2011. Documentation of the Oro Win language. Endangered Languages Archive, London. http://hdl.handle.net/2196/00-0000-0000-0000-A923-5
sources.note: 29 audio/video items (narratives, conversation, elicitation); no written sketch or phonology deposited.

sources.citation: Everett, Daniel L. 1994. New Language, New Sound, YES! LINGUIST List 5.1189 (28 Oct 1994). https://linguistlist.org/issues/5/5-1189/
sources.note: Nothing on stress; discussion of the [tʙ̥] sound and of Oro Win as a distinct Chapacuran language.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, Oro Win (orow1243), inventory SAPHON 1889. https://phoible.org/languages/orow1243
sources.note: Segment inventory only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Popky, Donna H. 1999. Oro Win: a descriptive and comparative look at an endangered language. MA thesis, University of Pittsburgh. 63 f.

sources.note: The only full phonological description of Oro Win (lexical phonology, 244 pp.); Birchall et al. 2016 and Birchall & Cabixi 2021 name it as the phonetic/phonological analysis of the language; a stress/accent section is near-certain. Not indexed in BDTD, CAPES or the UNIR repository; UNIR Guajará-Mirim library print.
